stories.title: The Points Guy Takes 12K SF at 875 Avenue of the Americas in NoMad
stories.excerpt: Travel media platform The Points Guy (TPG) has swiped its corporate card at 875 Avenue of the Americas, also known as One NoMad. The operator of the travel and lifestyle website leased 11,765 square feet at the 26-story office building, at the corner of Avenue of the Americas and West 31st Street in Manhattan’s NoMad neighborhood. TPG secured the space from landlords Kaufman Organization and Beacon Capital Partners at an asking rent of $85 per square foot, according to Kaufman. The lease term spans five years and six months. Traded first reported the deal. Kaufman’s Grant Greenspan, Michael Kaufman and Benjamin Saftler negotiated the deal on the landlord’s behalf, while Cushman & Wakefield’s Jonathan Fein and Brian Decillis represented TPG. “The Points Guy is exactly the kind of dynamic, forward-thinking company that One NoMad was designed to attract,” Greenspan, principal of Kaufman’s leasing company, told Commercial Observer. It was not immediately clear whether TPG plans to relocate from its offices at Sovereign Partners’ 100 Fifth Avenue, located one block west of Union Square. The travel media platform was launched in 2010 by its founder, Brian Kelly, to help spenders leverage their credit card points on travel. The company was most recently acquired by Red Ventures, a digital media and marketing company. Kaufman and Beacon recently invested $10 million in improvements at 875 Avenue of the Americas and rebranded the prewar building as One NoMad, CO reported last year. The renovations added features designed to attract media companies, including a private theater. Other tenants at the 265,000-square-foot tower include advertising network Firefly and digital workspace marketplace Instant Group. A spokesperson for C&W declined to comment, and representatives for TPG did not immediately respond to a request. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: The Points Guy leased 11,765 SF at 875 Avenue of the Americas (One NoMad) in Manhattan.
Rent: $85/SF on 5.5-year term; landlords are Kaufman Organization and Beacon Capital Partners.
Office leasing demand in NoMad persists despite broader Manhattan office headwinds.
stories.summary: Travel media platform The Points Guy signed an 11,765-square-foot lease at One NoMad in Manhattan's NoMad neighborhood at $85 per square foot for 5.5 years. The deal signals continued office demand from media and tech-forward tenants in the submarket. Landlords Kaufman Organization and Beacon Capital Partners secured the lease through their leasing team.
stories.impact: Limited direct impact on multifamily development. However, office lease activity in NoMad suggests sustained white-collar job concentration in Manhattan; successful office retention may stabilize or slow residential conversion opportunities in the neighborhood and keep rents elevated in nearby multifamily stock.

stories.title: Miami Design District Owner Revives Office Project With BH3
stories.excerpt: A dormant office project within the Miami Design District luxury mall is being resurrected with BH3 Management as a partner and about 40 percent more space. The project, called the Ursa, will feature 250,000 square feet of office space and 15,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space at 30 Northeast 39th Street, facing North Miami Avenue, near the southwest corner of the open-air Design District mall. Arquitectonica and the firm of famed artist Daniel Arsham designed the 20-story development. The owners of the 18-block retail center — a partnership between Craig Robins’s Dacra and the LVMH-backed private equity firm L Catterton Real Estate — and Fort Lauderdale-based BH3 plan to break ground next year, with completion slated for 2029. A representative for the project declined to comment on the Ursa’s pre-leasing. The Miami Design District owners unveiled plans for the Ursa in 2022, just as a slew of new-market companies began opening offices in Miami in the wake of the pandemic. The 15-story development called for 180,000 square feet of office space. But the partnership failed to land office tenants and construction financing. The half-acre site remained vacant. In this new iteration, the Ursa will expand to include the neighboring 11,417-square-foot parcel along North Miami Avenue, which is owned by BH3 Management, a prominent development firm that also has a debt arm. The Ursa is just one of the new developments in the pipeline at the Miami Design District, home to Chanel, Prada and Hermes boutiques. LLast week, another office development broke ground after securing a $125 million construction loan with signed leases from the private equity firm of billionaire Josh Harris and concierge medical service Atria Health Research. Another project underway includes a 25-story condo tower and a 12-story hotel, branded by luxury hotel Fouquet’s and designed by Pritzker Prize-winning architect David Chipperfield, though construction has yet to begin. bullets: Miami Design District (Dacra and L Catterton) reviving 250K SF office project 'Ursa' with BH3 Management.
Project: 20-story, 15K SF retail, groundbreaking 2026, completion 2029.
Signals office-to-multifamily conversion risk; retail-anchored office in luxury district competing for Miami investment capital.
stories.summary: The Ursa, a dormant office development in Miami's Design District, is being revived with 250,000 square feet of office space and 15,000 square feet of ground-floor retail on a 20-story tower designed by Arquitectonica and Daniel Arsham. Dacra, L Catterton Real Estate, and BH3 Management are partners, with groundbreaking targeted for 2026 and delivery in 2029. The project represents a 40 percent increase in density over the original concept.
stories.impact: In Miami Design District and broader luxury retail submarkets, revival of office-retail mixed-use projects may signal capital competition and diversion from multifamily into premium office; however, the 2029 delivery timeline and design-driven positioning suggest targeting flight-to-quality tenants, which could anchor neighborhood stability and support adjacent multifamily demand if office realizes strong pre-leasing.

stories.title: Joint Venture Launches Construction on Multifamily at Yonkers’ Ridge Hill Center
stories.excerpt: A joint venture of Saber-Hightower, Rafferty Real Estate and Eagle Realty Group has begun construction on The Ibex at Ridge Hill, a 17-story, 282-unit rental building at Ridge Hill, the open-air lifestyle center in Yonkers. Bank OZK is providing construction financing for the $140-million project. The building will include 28 affordable units. First units are expected to be available in late 2028. Designed by Beyer Blinder Belle, the building will be located directly adjacent to the Whole Foods Market on Ridge Hill’s Main Street. The project will also include 5,000 square feet of ground-floor retail and 423 resident parking spaces within Ridge Hill’s existing garage. “We are excited to become an important part of this world-class mixed-use center,” said Greg Belew, managing principal of Saber-Hightower. “Our residents will have the ability to walk out the door and enjoy a wide variety of dining, shopping, and entertainment options.” The post Joint Venture Launches Construction on Multifamily at Yonkers’ Ridge Hill Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Saber-Hightower, Rafferty, Eagle Realty broke ground on 282-unit The Ibex at Ridge Hill, Yonkers.
17-story, $140M project; 28 affordable units; Bank OZK financing; delivery late 2028.
Ridge Hill lifestyle center anchors suburban Westchester multifamily supply and absorption.
stories.summary: A joint venture of Saber-Hightower, Rafferty Real Estate, and Eagle Realty Group commenced construction on The Ibex at Ridge Hill in Yonkers—a 282-unit, 17-story rental building with 28 affordable units. Bank OZK provided $140 million in construction financing. The project is adjacent to Whole Foods within the Ridge Hill open-air lifestyle center and is scheduled for first move-ins in late 2028.
stories.impact: Strong supply signal for Yonkers and Westchester County rental market; Ridge Hill's mixed-use integration (retail, dining, Whole Foods proximity) de-risks leasing and supports premium rents, but 282 units delivery into a suburban market with regional inventory growth may pressure rate growth. Affordable component signals regulatory pressure in Westchester; monitor similar inclusionary mandates affecting project feasibility across the region.

stories.title: Erland Construction Partners with Nordblom on New Dedham Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Erland Construction has partnered with long-time client Nordblom Company on a new multifamily residential community, Vantage, in Dedham, MA. Working in collaboration with Stantec, Erland will construct a 218,000-square-foot, four-story wood- and steel-frame building with 155 apartment units. Built to align with Dedham’s stringent energy code standards, Vantage will include a fitness center, resident lounge, outdoor gathering spaces, and structured parking for 119 vehicles. The project scope also entails demolishing an existing building and site improvements to Stergis Way, supporting the Town of Dedham’s continued investment in smart, sustainable growth and resilient infrastructure. “We’re excited to once again collaborate with Erland and Stantec on this project,” said Patrick O’Neill, SVP at Nordblom. “Vantage represents more than just new housing. It’s an investment in sustainable design, quality craftsmanship, and community connectivity.” Scheduled for completion in Spring 2028, Vantage marks Erland’s fourth multifamily residential property with Nordblom. The post Erland Construction Partners with Nordblom on New Dedham Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Erland Construction and Nordblom broke ground on 155-unit Vantage in Dedham, MA.
218K SF, four-story, wood/steel frame; 119 parking spaces; completion Spring 2028.
Aligns with Dedham's energy and sustainable-growth priorities; existing demolition required.
stories.summary: Erland Construction and Nordblom Company launched construction on Vantage, a 155-unit, four-story multifamily community in Dedham, Massachusetts. The 218,000-square-foot project is designed to meet Dedham's energy code standards and includes fitness, resident amenities, and structured parking for 119 vehicles. Completion is scheduled for Spring 2028.
stories.impact: Boston-area suburban multifamily supply addition to competitive Dedham/inner-ring submarket. Tight energy code compliance and sustainable site improvements signal rising construction costs; monitor Dedham's zoning evolution and inclusionary policy for feasibility shifts. Nordblom's repeated partnership with Erland suggests stable developer economics in the market, but wood/steel hybrid construction and Spring 2028 delivery into a competitive market should be tracked for absorption trends.

stories.title: $100M Private Capital Effort Launched to Address Baltimore Vacant Housing Issues
stories.excerpt: The Greater Baltimore Committee (GCB) plans to launch a new Funders’ Consortium in November as part of its work with Enterprise Community Partners to develop a strategic investment framework. The initiative aims to align capital with a pipeline of projects and ultimately create a $100 million private fund to drive large-scale investment in Baltimore’s most challenged housing markets. These efforts complement the $1.2 billion in public funding already committed to address vacant housing in Baltimore. The Funders’ Consortium will bring public, private, and philanthropic funders together around a growing pipeline of redevelopment activity. The move aims to support projects with remaining financing gaps, aligning different sources of capital to advance them.The initiative builds on a partnership launched in December 2023 by GBC, Baltimoreans United in Leadership Development (BUILD) and the Mayor’s Office to address vacant and vulnerable properties. That work established a long-term strategy centered on more than $3 billion in public investment over 15 years, designed to address at least 37,000 properties and related infrastructure and leverage significant additional private investment. bullets: Greater Baltimore Committee launching $100M private funders' consortium for vacant housing redevelopment.
Builds on $1.2B public funding commitment; targets 37K properties over 15 years.
Private capital aggregation in distressed market signals risk-off repositioning and policy-driven development.
stories.summary: The Greater Baltimore Committee (GBC) is launching a Funders' Consortium in November to aggregate $100 million in private capital for large-scale housing redevelopment in Baltimore's most challenged markets. The effort complements $1.2 billion in public funding already committed and is part of a broader 15-year strategy to address 37,000 vacant and vulnerable properties, requiring an estimated $3 billion in total public investment.
stories.impact: Baltimore market signal: massive public subsidy underwriting private deployment suggests institutional-grade multifamily development requires policy support to achieve returns. Heavy reliance on public capital and organized funders' consortium indicates distressed property acquisition, conversion, and value-add strategies may be the only viable path; watch for competing capital to flow toward de-risked projects anchored by public funding. Entry-stage developers face high capital discipline and due-diligence burden; larger, policy-savvy operators better positioned to participate.

stories.title: Culver City Inks Purchase Option Agreement for Former Sony Animation Campus
stories.excerpt: Culver City’s City Council and Public Finance Authority unanimously approved a $103-million exclusive purchase option agreement with an entity tied to Fortress Investment Group for the former Sony Pictures Animation Campus at 9050 Washington Blvd. Fortress foreclosed on the property’s defaulted mortgage and took possession of the 198,000-square-foot complex for $71 million last month. The property was formerly owned by Hackman Capital Partners, which paid $160 million in 2021. Fortress bought out the approximately $104-million unpaid mortgage note before taking title to the property, according to Westside Today. The agreement between Culver City and CF CC Investor LLC gives the Public Finance Authority until February 2027 to determine whether to move forward with a purchase, the Culver City Observer reported. The property is being evaluated as part of a potential long-term economic development opportunity that could support public parking, recreation, tourism, job creation, new and diversified revenue sources, and future affordable or workforce housing opportunities. The post Culver City Inks Purchase Option Agreement for Former Sony Animation Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Culver City approved $103M exclusive purchase option for former Sony Animation Campus (198K SF).
Fortress foreclosed, owns property (paid $71M); option expires Feb 2027.
Municipal acquisition signals affordable/workforce housing and economic development redirection away from studio back-office.
stories.summary: Culver City's City Council and Public Finance Authority approved a $103 million exclusive purchase option agreement with Fortress Investment Group for the former Sony Pictures Animation Campus at 9050 Washington Boulevard. Fortress foreclosed on the 198,000-square-foot property last month after Hackman Capital Partners' default on a $104 million mortgage. The city has until February 2027 to exercise the option, with potential end-uses including affordable or workforce housing, public parking, recreation, and job creation.
stories.impact: Culver City multifamily opportunity: municipally-driven acquisition signals policy shift away from studio back-office toward affordable/workforce housing. If city exercises purchase, expect mixed-use redevelopment or conversion to residential. Fortress' distressed acquisition at $71M (vs. $160M Hackman paid in 2021) reflects studio real estate deterioration and potential opportunity for developers partnering with public entities. Monitor city's 2026-27 strategic decision; may trigger site release for third-party development or city-led RFP, opening acquisition or ground-lease partnerships in supply-constrained Culver City.

stories.title: AstraZeneca Plans $1-Billion Spend to Grow Massachusetts Presence
stories.excerpt: AstraZeneca plans to spend $1 billion to grow its workforce in Massachusetts by 50% over the coming years. The UK-based biopharmaceutical company has just opened a 570,000-square-foot R&D center in Cambridge’s Kendall Square, building on its oexisting presence in Cambridge and Boston. Together with its site for genomic medicine at 100 Binney St., the new AstraZeneca R&D Center Kendall Square at 290 Binney St. will be home to nearly 2,000 researchers and scientists who will accelerate the company’s oncology, cell therapy, chronic disease and rare disease pipeline. It includes ten floors of interconnecting laboratories. Pascal Soriot, CEO, AstraZeneca, said: “Kendall Square is a leading innovation ecosystem, and it is one of the key locations where AstraZeneca will discover the next generation of scientific breakthroughs. Our new R&D center not only reflects AstraZeneca’s long-term commitment to Massachusetts but also our belief in delivering U.S.-led innovation to patients around the world.” The post AstraZeneca Plans $1-Billion Spend to Grow Massachusetts Presence appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: AstraZeneca investing $1B to grow Massachusetts workforce 50% from Cambridge Kendall Square presence.
New 570K SF R&D center at 290 Binney Street; targeting ~2K researchers.
Major biotech expansion signals sustained high-wage job concentration and multifamily demand in Boston metro.
stories.summary: AstraZeneca announced a $1 billion commitment to expand its Massachusetts presence by 50 percent, anchored by a new 570,000-square-foot R&D center it just opened at 290 Binney Street in Cambridge's Kendall Square. The facility will house nearly 2,000 researchers and scientists across oncology, cell therapy, chronic disease, and rare disease programs. The investment reflects AstraZeneca's long-term commitment to Boston as a U.S. innovation hub.
stories.impact: Significant positive demand signal for Boston-area multifamily, especially Cambridge/Kendall Square and inner-ring neighborhoods. AstraZeneca's $1B spend and 50% workforce expansion (likely 1,000+ new high-wage jobs) will drive sustained inbound migration and rental demand in life-sciences-concentrated neighborhoods. Developers should prioritize transit-connected sites near Kendall Square and biotech clusters (Seaport, Longwood); expect sustained rent growth and premium pricing for walkable, amenity-rich product. Potential upward pressure on construction costs and labor competition in Boston market as pharma capex accelerates.

stories.title: Coworking Firm Nomadworks Inks 34K SF at Rosen’s 122 West 27th Street
stories.excerpt: Coworking operator Nomadworks has secured a new location in Manhattan’s Chelsea neighborhood. The 33,783-square-foot lease at 122 West 27th Street establishes Nomadworks’ fourth New York City location roughly two blocks west of Madison Square Park. The future coworking space will span the entire ninth, 10th and 11th floors of the Rosen family’s 12-story office building, according to Koeppel Rosen, the landlord’s leasing and management agent. “Nomadworks is excited to continue its growth, having successfully opened 295 Madison Avenue in late 2025,” Steven Cohen, Nomadworks’ CEO, told Commercial Observer. “We see Chelsea as a natural next step, as it has a very strong community of tech and artificial intelligence companies looking for high-quality communities, which we provide.” Koeppel Rosen’s Max Koeppel represented the landlord in the deal, which was first reported by CoStar. LSL Advisors negotiated on behalf of Nomadworks. The lease, signed in early September, comes with a 16-year term, and asking rent was $32 per square foot. New York-based Nomadworks got its start in 2018 at 1216 Broadway in Manhattan’s NoMad neighborhood. The company currently operates two other locations at 240 West 40th Street in Times Square and at 295 Madison Avenue near Grand Central Terminal. The latter location, which opened its doors last November, filled up in less than six months, Cohen said. Nomadworks’ three-floor spread at 122 West 27th Street will host its suite of private offices, coworking spaces and meeting rooms, according to Cohen, as well as event spaces. The company expects to take occupancy in late January. The 135,132-square-foot office building between Avenue of the Americas and Seventh Avenue is also occupied by event planner Van Wyck & Van Wyck, employment agency America Works of New York, Howell Belanger Castelli Architects and the offices of gallerist Eden Gallery. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Coworking firm Nomadworks leased 33,783 SF at 122 West 27th Street, Chelsea, Manhattan.
16-year lease; $32/SF asking; spans entire floors 9-11; fourth NYC location.
Coworking expansion signals fragmented office demand but also postive tech/AI tenant concentration in Chelsea.
stories.summary: Coworking operator Nomadworks signed a 33,783-square-foot lease at 122 West 27th Street in Manhattan's Chelsea neighborhood, occupying the entire 9th, 10th, and 11th floors on a 16-year term at $32 per square foot. This is Nomadworks' fourth New York City location and follows its late-2025 opening at 295 Madison Avenue. The company cited Chelsea's concentration of tech and artificial intelligence companies as a driver.
stories.impact: Mixed signal for Manhattan office and adjacent multifamily. Coworking leasing suggests flexible-space demand remains viable, but long-term (16-year) commitment at lower rent ($32/SF vs. $85/SF for traditional office) indicates flight to value and possible cannibalization of conventional office. However, Nomadworks' explicit targeting of tech/AI talent in Chelsea signals continued high-wage job concentration; this may support multifamily demand and rents in Chelsea and nearby neighborhoods, offsetting office weakness. Monitor coworking operators' tenant profile; if they anchor tech/creative hubs, multifamily developers should prioritize Chelsea, NoMad, and Flatiron submarkets for premium rental supply.

stories.title: L.A. Office Leasing Hits Highest Level Since 2019
stories.excerpt: Los Angeles County office leasing climbed to its highest level since 2019 during the third quarter in another sign that the market is slowly stabilizing. Tenants signed about 4 million square feet of office leases in July, August and September, up 15 percent from a year ago and 0.7 percent from the second quarter, according to Savills. Renewals drove the activity, accounting six of the quarter’s 10 largest deals. Raytheon signed the third quarter’s largest deal, renewing 144,709 square feet in El Segundo, followed by PwC’s 138,000-square-foot relocation to Century City and Pepperdine University’s 117,495-square-foot renewal near Marina del Rey and Playa Vista. Ad agency Innocean USA also relocated to 101,000 square feet in El Segundo. The leasing improvement comes with a decline in available space. Overall availability fell to 26.5 percent, down 110 basis points since the second quarter and 170 basis points from a year ago. Available sublease space fell to 6.3 million square feet from 8.7 million square feet last year for the eighth straight quarter of declining sublease supply. A lone pedestrian is seen reflected in the window of the Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce. PHOTO: Justin Sullivan/Getty Images The biggest improvements were in Century City, Beverly Hills and El Segundo, while several parts of L.A. still carry availability rates above 30 percent. Miracle Mile had the highest office availability at 39.2 percent, followed by Burbank at 37.1 percent and Culver City at 37 percent. Average asking rents slipped 0.2 percent from the second quarter but increased 0.6 percent since last year, while Class A rents rose 0.8 percent annually. Century City and Beverly Hills remained the market’s most expensive submarkets, with asking rents averaging $7.61 and $6.71 per square foot per month, respectively. Savills expects landlords in premier submarkets to retain pricing power as trophy space tightens, and concessions are likely to remain near historic highs. Gregory Cornf
bullets: L.A. County office leasing hit 4M SF in Q3 2024, highest since 2019; up 15% YoY.
Availability fell to 26.5% (down 110 bps QoQ); sublease fell to 6.3M SF from 8.7M YoY.
Renewals drove activity (6 of 10 largest deals); demand from tech, defense, education tenants.
stories.summary: Los Angeles County office leasing reached 4 million square feet in third quarter 2024, the highest level since 2019 and up 15 percent year-over-year. Available sublease space declined for the eighth consecutive quarter to 6.3 million square feet, and overall availability fell to 26.5 percent, down 110 basis points sequentially. Renewals drove activity, with major deals from Raytheon, PwC, Pepperdine, and Innocean USA in El Segundo, Century City, and Marina del Rey.
stories.impact: Stabilizing L.A. office market signals reduced conversion pressure on multifamily stock and supports rents in office-adjacent neighborhoods (Century City, El Segundo, Marina del Rey, Playa Vista). Sublease decline and tightening availability indicate less distressed space and improved landlord leverage, supporting office rents and reducing incentives for Class B/C conversion. However, activity remains renewal-heavy, not net new, suggesting limited organic job growth; multifamily developers should expect stable but not accelerating demand in L.A. submarkets. Monitor tech sector health; if ad agencies and tech tenants continue consolidating (Innocean relocation suggests industry churn), could signal white-collar instability and warrant caution on L.A. multifamily rent assumptions.

stories.title: Baltimore Organizations Line Up Financing for Stalled Housing Projects
stories.excerpt: Maryland city and state officials are looking to the public sector to turn back the clock on widespread urban decay in Baltimore. With the city and state already providing $1.2 billion, the Greater Baltimore Committee (GBC) is looking for an additional $100 million to help finance struggling real estate projects through a “funders’ consortium,” the organization announced Tuesday. The committee, led by GBC President and CEO Mark Anthony Thomas, is hoping to activate redevelopment of an estimated 11,800 vacant or abandoned houses as well as “tens of thousands” of vacant lots through the massive financing drive. It comes out to a total of about 37,000 properties, according to GBC. “This is an important next step in building the private sector support needed to strengthen Baltimore’s neighborhoods,” Thomas said in a statement. “For institutions looking to make an impact in Baltimore, this creates an opportunity to collaborate through GBC and support the projects and neighborhoods driving our revitalization. There is significant investment and activity already underway. We want to make it easier for capital providers to see those opportunities, work together, and help move projects that can strengthen neighborhood housing markets.” GBC is working with housing nonprofit Enterprise Community Partners to hammer out the details of its private capital strategy as well as its implementation, with the funds being made available primarily through financial institutions taking part in the program before the November launch. Organizations believe the financing will help projects in which the construction or rehabilitation costs of properties exceed the properties’ values, which seems to limit developers’ avenues for more conventional financing. bullets: Baltimore organizations (GBC, GCB, BUILD, Mayor) securing financing for stalled housing redevelopment projects.
Total strategy: $3B public investment over 15 years to address 37K properties.
Private funders' consortium ($100M) targeting 11,800 vacant/abandoned houses and tens of thousands of vacant lots.
stories.summary: Greater Baltimore Committee and city/state officials are organizing financing for stalled Baltimore housing redevelopment projects, building on $1.2 billion in public funding already committed. The GBC is spearheading a new funders' consortium to raise an additional $100 million in private capital as part of a broader 15-year, $3 billion public investment strategy to address an estimated 37,000 vacant or abandoned properties and related infrastructure.
stories.impact: Baltimore multifamily development heavily dependent on public subsidy and organized private capital deployment. Massive vacant property inventory and coordinated funders' consortium signal risk concentration and barrier to independent developer entry; only well-capitalized, policy-connected operators with access to consortium or direct public partnerships can compete. Expect conversion-heavy, affordability-focused, value-add-dominated development pipeline; traditional market-rate multifamily development unlikely to generate acceptable returns without significant public gap financing. Broader signal: baltimore's distressed property stock and subsidy reliance limit ROI for fee developers; prioritize markets with organic demand fundamentals over policy-driven redevelopment.
